svg.title: viber - from an idea to committed code
svg.desc: Flow diagram of the viber plugin: one-time setup, the optional triage of an issue and UI prototype, the two entries (an idea through the intent interview, which asks in rounds and saves the confirmed summary as a file, a bug through the fixer diagnosis), the planner reading that input, choosing the spec shape and writing the plan, the planner-review agent gating it, the approval gate you pass yourself (a plan written outside the planner is only reviewed, under the planning.outside-plan-review switch), then two ways out: a draft specification continued by a later interview round, or the implementor building the plan with task-coder, task-reviewer and one commit per task, its tasks in parallel where their dependencies allow, preceded, when build.baseline-tests is fast or full, by a baseline test run recording what already fails. The build closes with the final review, the fast tests plus the change's integration tests, which under build.baseline-tests treats only new failures as repair work, the optional memory, rules and QA writers, the project's own extension agents listed in build.extensions and the closeout that archives the run, followed later by the e2e pass that turns the QA scenarios into Playwright tests.
svg.text: From an idea to committed code
skill - runs in your own session
your call, or its switch is on
once per project - seeds .claude/viber.yml (the switches below), the .gitignore rules and the recommended permissions,
checks the gh CLI and that CLAUDE.md names your build and test commands, then opens the usage guide
Assesses one issue against your code: can it be done, how, how big.
Names the next step, runs nothing · issue number, URL or pasted text
New idea · feature · change to something existing
An HTML mockup of a UI change in your
project's own look, settled in conversation.
Asks in rounds, every decision with options and a recommendation.
Too big for one cycle? Split into ordered parts, every part discussed.
Ends in a summary you confirm, saved as a file for the planner.
github.issues on: can start from a GitHub issue or open a new one
Traces the bug to its root cause - no guessing.
Proves it with a failing test, left RED in your tree.
Never fixes it - the diagnosis goes to the planner.
github.issues on: can start from a GitHub issue
the diagnosis and its failing test
Writes the plan in plan mode, against your actual codebase.
Picks the spec shape; every task names its files, dependencies and verification.
asked to stop at a specification? it writes a draft instead
planning.adr on: adr-screener screens decisions; a record is a task with no dependencies
branching on: the plan names the git branch the run works on
one plan · numbered tasks · acceptance criteria
Reads the plan against the codebase before you ever see it.
PASS or FAIL - a FAIL sends the plan back for another round

no code is written before this, except fixer's reproduction test · a plan that failed review cannot leave plan mode · a plan written outside the planner is only reviewed (planning.outside-plan-review)
for you to commit and circulate.
the next round. A build refuses a draft.
BUILD - the approved plan, split into tasks
Lands the plan, splits it into task files, never writes code itself.
A task starts only once its dependencies are done.
independent ready tasks run side by side, an exclusive task runs alone
branching on: the run works on its own git branch
Baseline: runs the suite once before the first task
a red baseline: the arbiter rules to continue, in rulings.md
Builds one task and proves it green.
sees only its own task file, so it cannot drift into another task's files
5 attempts, a repair pass, then the arbiter; rulings go to rulings.md
Checks the task against what the plan said it must do.
skipped only when a sonnet task's check runs your build or tests
a finding goes to the coder for 5 attempts, a repair pass, the arbiter
the subject comes from the plan · only that task's files are staged
Reviews the finished build past each task's own diff,
one reviewer per slice of up to 8 tasks.
each fix is rechecked; a failed recheck goes to the arbiter
Runs the build, fast tests, the change's integration tests.
a failure goes to a repair coder, up to 5 rounds, then the arbiter rules
build.baseline-tests fast or full: only new failures go to repair
only the switches you turned on
Your CLAUDE.md learns what the build taught.
every file kept under its size cap
a fact about one place goes to CLAUDE.md instead
Test scenarios for what was actually delivered:
a checklist for a person, a handoff for /viber:e2e
Your own agents from .claude/agents/, run in the listed order.
one commit per agent; a failure never stops the archive
Notes on the specification what the build delivered beyond it,
then moves the run into the archive, in one commit.
keeps the specification and the QA documents - git keeps the rest
later, when you want them automated
Turns the QA scenarios into Playwright tests.
runs them against your application, commits the ones that pass
